A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DNO research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and support comparison despite title changes and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original toy-distribution and image-generation experiments, including reward optimization, regularization ablations, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds Best-of-N results, image–text matching measurements, and a diffusion-step study.

M1.justification: The noise optimization objective, probability regularizer, DDIM-based procedure, and Hybrid-1/Hybrid-2 estimators remain unchanged. PRNO is relabeled DNO in Table 1; the added diffusion-step sweep tests an existing sampler setting.

E1.justification: The toy distributions, animal-prompt image tasks, SDXL examples, human-preference rewards, and JPEG-compressibility task are retained. Brightness and darkness rename the existing whiteness and blackness objectives; the background-generation discussion introduces no new evaluated scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Best-of-N sampling as an evaluated comparator. SD v1.5, LGD, SPIN, DDPO, and AlignProp remain, and Section 5.3 retains ZO-SGD and the hybrid estimators.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 adds Image-Text Matching (ITM) alongside CLIP Score. Section 5.2 introduces a ten-minute Best-of-N budget and a one-minute DNO evaluation varying diffusion steps across 10, 15, 20, 25, and 50 while holding other hyperparameters fixed. The retained Table 1 experiments use 50 diffusion steps.

E4.justification: New Table 2 examines the diffusion-step versus optimization-time tradeoff under a fixed budget. ITM adds another diagnostic to the existing regularization analysis. The ODE/SDE comparison, hybrid-gradient comparisons, and appendix sensitivity and failure-case analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experimental figures report means and standard deviations over 1,000 random seeds. v3 extends the existing reporting practice to additional curves without reporting a change in run counts or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains the one-, three-, and five-minute DNO scores but replaces its ten-minute DNO column (10.68, 0.354, 25.16) with Best-of-N results (6.531, 0.298, 22.09), ordered as Aesthetic, HPS, and PickScore. These are different methods, not a performance decline. New Table 2 reports step-dependent results, including 7.496, 0.341, and 24.82 at 15 steps. Figure 6 adds ITM curves supporting prompt preservation with regularization.

T1.justification: Theorem 1, the ODE/SDE comparison derivation, concentration inequalities, gradient-estimator mathematics, and Appendix B proofs and stationary-point cases are retained. Removing duplicated explanatory prose does not change the mathematics.

C1.justification: v3 narrows the introduction's aim from achieving or outperforming tuning-based methods to matching them at reasonable additional inference cost. It removes the abstract's explicit high-image-quality claim and the contribution statement's comparison against all existing methods. The central methodological contributions remain.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 newly presents bright/dark background generation as a practical application and relates it to Offset-Noise fine-tuning. Section 5.2 explicitly acknowledges that three to five minutes may be prohibitive and discusses fewer diffusion steps as mitigation. The earlier assertion that early stopping cannot replicate regularization is removed.

D1.justification: The implementation link and Appendix D's checkpointing instructions, optimizer settings, regularization coefficients, gradient-estimation parameters, hardware, and memory disclosures remain unchanged. No new implementation or resource-access information accompanies the added evaluation protocols.

R1.justification: v3 adds CrossLabs (2023), Diffusion with Offset Noise, and positions regularized DNO as obtaining bright/dark backgrounds without that fine-tuning approach. The existing cited research is otherwise retained.

P1.justification: The title changes from Tuning-Free to Inference-Time Alignment. Terminology and several introduction and experiment paragraphs are revised, the mapping-comparison explanation is removed, and duplicated discussion after Theorem 1 is condensed. The section and appendix organization remains substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2's conceptual Figure 2 is removed, while its procedure diagram becomes v3 Figure 2. The regularization plot expands from six to eight panels, Table 1 changes column grouping, and Table 2 is added. Figure 1 labels and figure placement change; other visual evidence is retained.

improvement.justification: Best-of-N supplies a relevant missing comparison, the fixed-budget step study strengthens the practical efficiency evidence, and ITM supplements the prompt-consistency analysis. More cautious performance wording also improves claim calibration. These gains outweigh the limited loss of the conceptual diagram and ten-minute DNO table entries, while the method, theory, and underlying task coverage remain unchanged.
